1: /**
2:  * Model接入 Catalog — declarative provider templates (design doc:
3:  * docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-11-model-catalog-design.md).
4:  *
5:  * A {@link CatalogEntry} is a *template* the user can pick in the 连接 page to
6:  * create a configured instance (stored in settings.imageGen/videoGen.providers[]).
7:  * Catalog = "能配哪些"; providers[] = "配了哪些". The two are decoupled.
8:  *
9:  * For text entries, `adapterKind` is the provider/gateway capability identity
10:  * ("openai"/"openrouter"/"deepseek"/…), while `protocol` selects the wire
11:  * client. For image/video it remains the concrete runtime adapter selector
12:  * ("openai"/"google"/"fal"). `shape` is documentation/future only.
13:  */
14: 
15: import { z } from "zod";
16: 
17: const id = z.string().min(1).max(128);
18: const shortText = z.string().max(256);
19: const longText = z.string().max(32_768);
20: const boundedNumber = z.number().finite().min(0).max(1_000_000_000);
21: 
22: /**
23:  * How the param maps onto the outgoing request body. `field` is the request
24:  * field this param lands on — same param name can land differently per
25:  * adapter (reasoning → `reasoning_effort` on OpenAI vs
26:  * `thinking.budget_tokens` on Anthropic), so the divergence lives in data, not
27:  * in `if (kind === ...)` branches in the engine. Minimal v1: field only.
28:  */
29: export const wireSpecSchema = z.object({
30:   field: id,
31: });
32: 
33: /**
34:  * One **generic** declarative param — no special-casing per param. reasoning
35:  * is not its own variant: it's `control: "enum"` (OpenAI effort levels) or
36:  * `control: "number"` (Anthropic token budget), decided by the entry's data.
37:  * The connection page renders by `switch(control)`; `doc` is woven into the
38:  * tool description so the agent knows what a configured model accepts.
39:  * See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-15-unified-model-catalog-design.md §3.2.
40:  */
41: export const paramSpecSchema = z.object({
42:   /** Logical name, e.g. "reasoning" / "size" / "quality" / "temperature". */
43:   name: id,
44:   /** UI control label (falls back to `name`). */
45:   label: shortText.optional(),
46:   control: z.enum(["enum", "number", "toggle", "text"]),
47:   /** control=enum allowed values, e.g. ["low","medium","high","xhigh"]. */
48:   options: z.array(shortText).max(64).optional(),
49:   /** control=number bounds. */
50:   min: boundedNumber.optional(),
51:   max: boundedNumber.optional(),
52:   default: z.union([shortText, boundedNumber, z.boolean()]).optional(),
53:   /** Natural-language usage note → injected into the tool description. */
54:   doc: z.string().max(4_096).optional(),
55:   /** How this param lands on the request body. */
56:   wire: wireSpecSchema.optional(),
57: });
58: 
59: export type ParamSpec = z.infer<typeof paramSpecSchema>;
60: 
61: /**
62:  * A known model under an entry, carrying its own param schema
63:  * (per-entry-per-model — the same modelId via OpenRouter vs the official API
64:  * can expose different params, since gateways normalize differently).
65:  */
66: export const modelPresetSchema = z.object({
67:   value: id,
68:   label: shortText.optional(),
69:   maxContextTokens: boundedNumber.optional(),
70:   maxOutputTokens: boundedNumber.optional(),
71:   supportsVision: z.boolean().optional(),
72:   /** Params this model supports; absent → no adjustable knobs. */
73:   params: z.array(paramSpecSchema).max(64).optional(),
74: });
75: 
76: export type ModelPreset = z.infer<typeof modelPresetSchema>;

42:  * EXPLICITLY (not via paramSpecsFromCapability) because the capability layer's
43:  * OpenRouter catch-all would slap reasoning onto *every* model — including ones
44:  * that don't support it. A reasoning OpenRouter preset opts in by listing this.
45:  */

49:   control: "enum",

51:   default: "medium",
52:   doc: "Reasoning effort — how hard the model thinks before answering.",
53:   wire: { field: "reasoning.effort" },
54: };

1: import { updateScopedSettings } from "./settingsAuthority";
2: 
3: /**
4:  * Settings change broadcast.
5:  *
6:  * The worker (agent-server-stdio) keeps its own SettingsManager
7:  * instance; without an explicit reload it ignores edits the user
8:  * makes through the settings page. The "codeshell:settings-changed"
9:  * event is App.tsx's signal to dispatch configure({reloadModels:
10:  * true}) at the worker. Every successful settings write must fire
11:  * the event — historically callers forgot, which is exactly the
12:  * "project-level settings 不生效" bug from TODO-week.md #3.
13:  *
14:  * This helper centralises the dispatch so call sites just go through
15:  * `writeSettings(...)` and don't have to remember.
16:  */
17: 
18: export function notifySettingsChanged(): void {
19:   window.dispatchEvent(new Event("codeshell:settings-changed"));
20: }
21: 
22: export async function writeSettings(
23:   scope: "user" | "project",
24:   patch: Record<string, unknown>,
25:   projectPath?: string,
26: ): Promise<void> {
27:   await updateScopedSettings(scope, patch, projectPath);
28:   notifySettingsChanged();
29: }
